title: Desalvo–Pak ratio conjecture for the partition function
statement:
Let $p(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$. **Desalvo–Pak's conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq45$, 

$$
\frac{p(n-1)}{p(n)}\left(1+\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{24}n^{3/2}}\right)>\frac{p(n)}{p(n+1)}.
$$

The coefficient $\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{24}}$ is asymptotically best possible, and the conjecture was subsequently proved by Chen, Wang, and Xie.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.02558

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2015). “The log-convexity of $\{\sqrt[n]{p(n)}\}_{n\geq27}$ was conjectured by Sun . He also proposed the conjecture that $\{\sqrt[n]{p(n)}\}_{n\geq6}$ is strictly decreasing, which has been proved by Wang and Zhu .”
source_name: William Y. C. Chen and Ken Y. Zheng, “The Log-Behavior of [n]p(n) and [n]p(n)/n”, arXiv:1511.02558 (2015).
